output.brief: The likely cause is contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique or the new pads. Northfield Motor Services used an old, open bulk drum of fluid while Eastgate's own brake bay was closed. Two vans it re-tested had fluid boiling at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. All 11 vans with complaints were serviced at Northfield, and 11 of the 13 Northfield vans, all from the old drum, are the ones that complained. The same drivers had no brake problems in other vans, including on Upper Wend, and every van ran the hills about equally. Millbrook and Harrow Lane had almost no reports, so easier reporting doesn't explain it. Northfield's 25 Sep recommendation to recheck the other vans got no reply. Do this week: pull every van Northfield serviced before 10 Sep, test and renew the fluid from sealed stock, then return them to the pool. Do not issue warnings. Drivers' reports were accurate, and punishing them would suppress safety information. Hold off on switching pad supplier until you have clean evidence. The pad evidence is confounded and doesn't point to a fault. I'm fairly confident, about 85%. Two vans on the newer drum haven't been tested, so test them too.
